messages:
elaine: urgent - multiple customers reporting duplicate external actions (confirmation emails + double billing) when model triggers the 'send_email' tool. Happening intermittently across regions, started ~09:10 UTC. Need triage now. repro attached.

sam: can you paste an example request + headers + the API response? also customer id and request id if available.

elaine: repro curl below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-2","input":"Send confirmation","tools":["send_email"],"max_tokens":256}'
```
response: `202 Accepted` with body `\{\"status\":\"queued\", \"task_id\":\"t-9ab3\"}`
customer then saw network timeout on client and retried the whole request -> two emails sent. no `Idempotency-Key` header present.

nisha: do we have logs for task_id t-9ab3? any duplicate executions on the workers?

sam: digging logs: two separate tool_execute events within 12s: `tool_exec.start task=t-9ab3 run=run-77` and `tool_exec.start task=t-9ab3 run=run-78` (different run ids). Both completed. Gateway logs show initial 202 then client retried due to TLS timeout. Our gateway/ingest accepted the retried request as a fresh request because there was no idempotency key.

mike: hunch - token refresh path may be replaying the original model->tool invocation without preserving a dedupe key. Are any middlewares doing transparent replays after 401/expired token?

elaine: customers report token expiry shortly after issuance (short TTL). Our edge will request a refresh and then re-issue the upstream request in some cases. I think the sequence was: 1) client sends request with short token, 2) edge returns 202 but connection drops, 3) client retries, 4) edge still refreshes token or replays request path and ends up executing the tool handler again.

nisha: root causes look like (a) lack of idempotency header, (b) gateway/edge replay semantics that treat retried requests as new without checking dedupe store, (c) async 202 semantics confusing clients into retrying.

sam: quick repro for infra: simulate an expired token + forced client retry:
```
# simulate: first request returns 202 and then drop conn, client retries whole payload
# use curl with --max-time to force timeout and then rerun same curl (no idempotency header)
curl --max-time 1 -X POST ... (first) || true
sleep 1
curl -X POST ... (second)
```
logs: you should see two `tool_exec.start` events.

mike: mitigation plan (short term):
- SDK: add and surface `Idempotency-Key` automatically for generate/tool requests (UUID per logical request).
- Edge: if incoming request lacks idempotency key, compute deterministic hash of `{user_id, model, trimmed_input, tools}` and use as dedupe key for 30s. Check dedupe store before executing tool.
- Support: advise customers to avoid blind retries on 202 (treat as accept-in-progress).

infra-bot: created issue INFRA-4892 and pinned logs at https://internal.redwood/logs/trace/t-9ab3

dev-bot: rolling hotfix candidate to staging (patch: add middleware dedupe check; preserve `x-idempotency-key` if present).

elaine: deployed hotfix to staging and ran repro script — observed single `tool_exec.start` now; pushing to canary in us-west.

nisha: can support reach out to impacted customers to offer refunds for duplicate charges and explain SDK workaround? (cc @mike)

mike: yes. I'll coordinate refunds and a short support note: 1) upgrade SDK to include idempotency, 2) if you see 202 treat as in-progress and wait 30s before retrying, 3) contact support for manual refund if duplicates occurred.

elaine: monitoring on canary shows no new duplicates for last 20m. closing incident when canary finishes 2h window. thanks all :thumbsup:
